served.stem: In a community with three trophic levels (producers, primary consumers, secondary consumers), the introduction of a top predator (a tertiary consumer) typically results in:
choices: Trophic cascade; secondary-consumer numbers decline, primary consumers rebound, producer biomass decreases
Trophic cascade; secondary-consumer numbers decline, primary consumers also decline, producer biomass INCREASES
No effect; the new predator only eats producers
Loss of primary consumers across the food web
served.bankWhy: Adding a tertiary predator triggers a top-down trophic cascade: the new predator suppresses secondary consumers, which releases primary consumers from predation pressure (primary consumers rebound), and the increased primary-consumer grazing then reduces producer biomass. Option A describes this classic four-level cascade correctly.

answer.text: Trophic cascade; secondary-consumer numbers decline, primary consumers rebound, producer biomass decreases
answer.line: The new predator pushes each level below it the other way in turn: down, up, down.

steps: Start at the top and trace one level at a time. The new predator eats the secondary consumers, so they decline.
Fewer secondary consumers means less predation on the primary consumers. Released, they rebound.
More grazers eat more plants, so producer biomass falls. The pattern alternates all the way down.

choices.text: Trophic cascade; secondary-consumer numbers decline, primary consumers rebound, producer biomass decreases
choices.note: Down, up, down: each level flips the one below it.

choices.text: Trophic cascade; secondary-consumer numbers decline, primary consumers also decline, producer biomass INCREASES
choices.note: The cascade and the drop in secondary consumers are right. But prey rise when their predator falls, so primary consumers rebound and the plants lose.

choices.text: No effect; the new predator only eats producers
choices.note: An animal that eats producers is a primary consumer by definition. A tertiary consumer eats secondary consumers, and that starts the cascade.

choices.text: Loss of primary consumers across the food web
choices.note: Eating herbivores is what secondary consumers do. The new top predator eats the secondary consumers instead, which spares the herbivores.
This stops at "predators lower numbers" and paints every level with it. Trace the chain and the effects alternate.
